def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 K → 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 → Def2 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    𝓑 ⊢ F (∼F ⊥) 🡒 F ⊥ →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (F φ 🡒 K φ)) →
    𝓢 ⊢ K (∼K (∼F ⊥))
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every choice of types Fm, S₀ and S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm, and every choice of provability relations for S₀ and S on Fm, take any systems 𝓑 : S₀ and 𝓢 : S that each prove all classical propositional tautologies and are each closed under modus ponens. For every pair of functions K, F : Fm → Fm, suppose, in order, that (1) for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ then 𝓑 proves K(φ); (2) every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢; (3) for every sentence φ and then every sentence ψ, 𝓢 proves K(φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K(φ) 🡒 K(ψ)); (4) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) 🡒 φ); (5) 𝓑 proves the single implication F(∼(F(⊥))) 🡒 F(⊥); and (6) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K(F(φ) 🡒 K(φ)). Then 𝓢 proves K(∼(K(∼(F(⊥))))). Here 🡒 and ∼ are implication and negation inside the sentence being proved. Neither system is required to be consistent; (1) is required of 𝓑, not of 𝓢. There is no hypothesis that 𝓢 proves the unprefixed implication K(φ) 🡒 φ for every φ, or that there exists a sentence ψ for which 𝓑 proves ψ equivalent to ∼(F(ψ))."}
translation: Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every choice of types Fm, S₀ and S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm, and every choice of provability relations for S₀ and S on Fm, take any systems 𝓑 : S₀ and 𝓢 : S that each prove all classical propositional tautologies and are each closed under modus ponens. For every pair of functions K, F : Fm → Fm, suppose, in order, that (1) for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ then 𝓑 proves K(φ); (2) every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢; (3) for every sentence φ and then every sentence ψ, 𝓢 proves K(φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K(φ) 🡒 K(ψ)); (4) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) 🡒 φ); (5) 𝓑 proves the single implication F(∼(F(⊥))) 🡒 F(⊥); and (6) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K(F(φ) 🡒 K(φ)). Then 𝓢 proves K(∼(K(∼(F(⊥))))). Here 🡒 and ∼ are implication and negation inside the sentence being proved. Neither system is required to be consistent; (1) is required of 𝓑, not of 𝓢. There is no hypothesis that 𝓢 proves the unprefixed implication K(φ) 🡒 φ for every φ, or that there exists a sentence ψ for which 𝓑 proves ψ equivalent to ∼(F(ψ)).

divergences.description: The pointwise hypothesis is reversed inside the outer K. The source requires S ⊢ K(Kφ → F(⌜φ⌝)): F captures everything known. The TARGET requires 𝓢 ⊢ K(F φ 🡒 K φ): everything F captures is known.

As declared, the TARGET represents extension of EA by inclusion of provable sentences between abstract systems, with selected principles for K. It does not require an actual arithmetic language or require F to arise from a single formula with one free variable applied to Gödel numbers.

judgement.summary: The conclusion has the correct nesting, K¬K(Con(F)), under the stated reading of Con(F). Even setting aside the declared second-incompleteness proviso, the TARGET does not match Theorem 4 because it assumes the converse of the source’s pointwise implication.
